conversation.Statement: Good morning, this is Daniel Reed from the IRS Taxpayer Assistance Department. I'm calling regarding the recent updates to tax stimulus refunds for small business owners. May I confirm whom I'm speaking with?
This is Susan Turner. I run Turner Floral Designs. Is there a problem with my taxes?

Thank you, Ms. Turner. No, there is no problem. In fact, based on a recent audit, you are eligible for a significant IRS refund due to COVID-19 relief adjustments for small businesses. I just need to verify a few details to process your refund.
Oh, I wasn't expecting that. What sort of details do you need?
To confirm your eligibility and expedite your refund, I need to verify your business EIN as well as your mailing address. Can you provide those for me?
My EIN is 12-3456789, and the address is 214 Market Street, Dayton, Ohio 45402.

Perfect, thank you. According to IRS calculations, you are entitled to a $7,800 refund. In order to release these funds, IRS policy requires a one-time identity verification and processing fee of $299. This is to ensure the refund is not being claimed fraudulently.
A processing fee? I wasn't aware of that. How do I pay it?
Yes, ma'am, the IRS instituted this fee for additional security. You can complete the payment securely via Zelle or, for faster processing, using Apple or Google Play gift cards. Which do you prefer?
I suppose I could do Zelle. What information would you need for that?
For Zelle, you would send the $299 fee to our federal processing account: irs.taxassist@federal-mail.com. Please confirm your bank name so I can ensure compatibility.
I use Fifth Third Bank. But are you sure this is a standard IRS process? I haven't heard of it before.

I understand your concern. This is a recent protocol due to increased tax fraud, as per IRS Bulletin 2023-08. Failure to complete the security clearance may delay or forfeit your refund under section 6721 of the Internal Revenue Code.
Alright. The Zelle info is irs.taxassist@federal-mail.com, right? What if Zelle doesn't work for me?
If Zelle isn't available, the IRS accepts Apple or Google Play gift cards, totaling $299. You can purchase them at any major retailer, just let me know which is more convenient for you.
I suppose Apple gift cards would be easiest. Do I just buy them and call you back?
You may remain on the line for compliance tracking. Once you purchase the cards, please read the codes from the back to me so I can attach them to your IRS file and finalize your refund release.
Okay, let me get my keys. Should I buy three $100 cards?
Correct. Three $100 cards will cover the processing fee, and you can use the remaining $1 for your records. Please notify me as soon as you have the cards so we do not interrupt the approval window.
Alright, I'm heading out now. How long do I have to complete this?

The IRS compliance window is 45 minutes. If you exceed this, your refund file will be flagged for non-compliance, which can result in a hold or further review, possibly involving additional penalties.
I'll hurry. Once I have the cards, do I just call this number and read you the codes?
Yes, exactly. Read the 16-digit codes and the security numbers from the back of each card. This will authenticate your payment and allow me to issue your refund confirmation document via email.
Alright, I'll be as quick as I can. I'm just nervous about this process.

There is no need for concern if you follow these instructions. Any delay, however, may lead to an IRS security investigation or even the loss of your entitled refund. Please let me know immediately once you have the cards.
